construct: Normal aging is associated with progressive stiffening and reduced compliance of large arteries. Earlier return of reflected pressure waves augments systolic pressure, while reduced elastic recoil contributes to a wider pulse pressure and less effective buffering of abrupt hemodynamic changes.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A healthy older adult with progressively wider pulse pressure and no high-output or valvular explanation is best explained by normal age-related large-artery stiffening and reduced compliance, which causes earlier reflected pressure waves and greater systolic augmentation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Aortic compliance normally decreases, not increases. Generalized loss of arteriolar tone does not explain the characteristic widening of pulse pressure; baroreceptor sensitivity declines rather than rises; myocardial aging tends toward fibrosis and reduced diastolic compliance.
